title: Theme scopes and dark/light themes
learningObjectives: Explain theme scopes and dark/light themes and organise styles for maintainability.

understand.concept: Theme scopes apply design tokens to a region or the whole document. A light and dark theme can be represented by different custom-property values on a root element or a theme container. prefers-color-scheme can provide a default while an explicit user choice may override it.
understand.whyItMatters: Theme changes should preserve contrast, focus visibility, form control clarity, and user preference. Do not simply invert every colour; review semantic roles such as text, surface, border, and status.
understand.analogy: A theme is a coordinated palette of named roles, not a filter placed over the whole interface.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS cascade, inheritance, and conditional rules follow the formal cascade and at-rule processing model.

explain.narrative: The dark theme overrides token values within its scope; components use the same semantic token names.

questions.prompt: What is a benefit of theme-scoped custom properties?
options: Components can use the same semantic tokens under different palettes
questions.answer: Components can use the same semantic tokens under different palettes
questions.explanation: Theme scopes allow components to consume shared token names while values vary by context.

options: Make ownership, precedence, and reuse clear
Increase selector depth for every component
questions.answer: Make ownership, precedence, and reuse clear
questions.explanation: Clear organisation reduces accidental coupling and makes style changes easier to reason about.
